thread:
lia: Heads up — ACME reporting p99 spikes (~3.2s) since ~09:10 UTC. They say this started after a sustained traffic bump, and some requests show delayed token generation, not 5xx.
ops-bot: [alert] tenant=ACME p99 latency 3200ms, gpu-mem-usage=93%, kv-evicts=low, slab-frag=high
sam: Thanks, lia. Can you grab a tenant trace and the /metrics snapshot? Also what's the model + variant and route they hit?
lia: Route is /v1/generate -> model: gpt-j-6B-quant-v2, batch_hint=auto. Attached excerpt from trace: "token_emit_delay" spikes around 600–800ms per chunk for several requests.
devon: That model/quant combo is known to be sensitive to KV growth on 48GB nodes. Any KV cache size overrides?
maria: Not from ACME config — they use defaults.
sam: Ok. Lia, please run these on an affected worker and paste outputs:
```
curl -s http://metrics-worker:9100/metrics | egrep 'gpu_mem_used|kv_cache_size|kv_eviction'
redwoodctl runtime inspect --node <node> --json | jq '.allocator, .kv_stats'
```
lia: Pasting snippets:
```
# metrics
gpu_mem_used_bytes{node="gpu-12",} 49802300000
kv_cache_bytes{tenant="ACME",} 16543200000
kv_evictions_total{tenant="ACME",} 123
```
And alloc stats: "slab_frag_pct": "28.4", "free_chunks": "12", "total_kv_objects": "1.9M"
devon: 28% slab fragmentation + 16.5GB KV is high for a single tenant — we're seeing slowly creeping KV that fragments allocator state, causing many small allocs and per-token jitter. Repro steps please: an example curl that reproduces p99?
lia: Customer supplied repro:
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-j-6B-quant-v2","input":"<long chat history + repeated context>"}'
```
They noted it only happens for sessions with long history + frequent partial updates.
sam: Action plan: short-term mitigation, medium-term fixes, and follow-up items. Short-term: 1) Route ACME to lower-memory variant (gpt-j-6B-quant-small) for 2–4hrs, 2) enable aggressive KV eviction for tenant via feature-flag: `tenant.kv.eviction_mode=aggressive`, 3) restart the hottest worker after draining active sessions.
devon: Also reduce max_batch_tokens on the route: `route.max_batch_tokens=512` — reduces per-request working set. That helps reduce allocator pressure.
maria: Is there a risk of quality drop for ACME? They'll lose some context when we evict KV aggressively. Need to warn them.
sam: I'll coordinate with account. Lia can you apply the route override and flag, and then run a 30m synthetic that mimics the repro while we watch metrics?
lia: On it. Applying flags now. Running synthetic with 10 concurrent clients hitting long-history sessions.
ops-bot: [action] start draining node gpu-12 (active_sessions=42)
lia: Synthetic run shows p99 drop from 3.2s -> 850ms after moving tenant to smaller model + eviction. KV cache shows steady drop to ~4.2GB.
devon: Good. We should still schedule an allocator tuning: increase slab coalesce window and lower minimum chunk size to reduce fragmentation, and add a periodic defrag sweep. I can open an RFC/PR with suggested params.
sam: Medium-term: add telemetry alert for per-tenant kv_growth_rate and slab_frag_pct >20% for >15m, auto-route to fallback variant if threshold hit.
maria: Customer comms: I'll message ACME with mitigation notice and ask for acceptance of temporary context reduction.
lia: Customer replied: "We saw immediate improvement, thanks. Please keep us posted on permanent fix."
devon: Follow-ups for eng-runtime: 1) PR for allocator tuning + canary on internal fleet, 2) add tenant-level kv quotas + soft eviction watermark, 3) investigate KV compaction at checkpoint.
sam: I'll file support ticket and link to this thread. Lia — include the metric dumps and synthetic logs in the ticket.
lia: Uploaded artifacts to ticket #SUP-12984 and pinged account.
maria: I'll schedule a postmortem with ACME next week to discuss tradeoffs.
ops-bot: [note] scheduled rolling restart of gpu-12 in 10m window after drain complete.
sam: Great work team. Keep this thread updated if p99 creeps back up or if any regressions after allocator changes. :thumbsup:
